=={{header|Omegese}}==
{{works with|omc|sha256 2c824805, aien-dev/omega-mv e5b32567, Linux AArch64}}
Omega has no imports, so the small output helpers (<code>emit</code> and friends) are part of the program.
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
om2
text nl "\n"
text hexd "0123456789abcdef"
note K[i] = floor(abs(sin(i + 1)) * 2^32) as 64 eight-digit hex words (RFC 1321, section 3.4)
text khex ""
note the rotate amounts of the four rounds, two decimal digits each
text rots "07121722050914200411162306101521"
text m0 "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog"
text m1 "The quick brown fox jumped over the lazy dog's back"
text m2 "Rosetta Code"
text m3 "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa"
global kt uint 64
global hs uint 4
global mw uint 16
global buf uchar 128
note emit writes every byte of a to stdout; a short write is retried, an error exits 1
fn emit a view uchar * to void
o = ulong 0
while lt o len a bound 4096
k = write 1 a o sub len a o
if le k 0
exit 1
end
o = add o ulong k
end
end
note emitc writes one byte
fn emitc c uchar to void
b = new uchar 1 0
put b 0 c
emit b
end
note hexv gives the value of one lower-case hex digit
fn hexv c uchar to uint
if le c 57
ret uint sub c 48
end
ret uint sub c 87
end
note emith writes the byte v as two lower-case hex digits
fn emith v uchar to void
emitc get hexd shr v 4
emitc get hexd and v 15
end
fn initk to void
for i ulong 64
v = uint 0
for j ulong 8
v = or shl v 4 hexv get khex add mul i 8 j
end
put kt i v
end
end
note rotamt is the rotate amount of step i: round i / 16, place i mod 4
fn rotamt i ulong to uint
x = mul add mul div i 16 4 rem i 4 2
h = sub get rots x 48
l = sub get rots add x 1 48
ret uint add mul h 10 l
end
note rnd is step i of 64 on the state (a, b, c, d) in hs, with the block's words in mw
fn rnd i ulong to void
a = get hs 0
b = get hs 1
c = get hs 2
d = get hs 3
f = uint 0
g = ulong 0
if lt i 16
f = or and b c and not b d
g = i
else
if lt i 32
f = or and d b and not d c
g = rem add mul i 5 1 16
else
if lt i 48
f = xor xor b c d
g = rem add mul i 3 5 16
else
f = xor c or b not d
g = rem mul i 7 16
end
end
end
f = add add add f a get kt i get mw g
s = rotamt i
put hs 0 d
put hs 3 c
put hs 2 b
put hs 1 add b rotl f s
end
note block loads the 64 bytes of buf at p as 16 little-endian words and runs the 64 steps
fn block p ulong to void
for w ulong 16
v = uint 0
for j ulong 4
v = or shl v 8 uint get buf add add p mul w 4 sub 3 j
end
put mw w v
end
sv = new uint 4 0
for k ulong 4
put sv k get hs k
end
for i ulong 64
rnd i
end
for k ulong 4
put hs k add get hs k get sv k
end
end
note md5 pads a (up to 119 bytes) with 0x80, zeros and the bit length (little-endian) to one or two
note 64-byte blocks, hashes them and prints the digest in hex
fn md5 a view uchar * to void
put hs 0 uint 1732584193
put hs 1 uint 4023233417
put hs 2 uint 2562383102
put hs 3 uint 271733878
n = len a
for i ulong 128
put buf i 0
end
for i ulong n
put buf i get a i
end
put buf n 128
t = ulong 64
if ge n 56
t = 128
end
bits = mul n 8
for j ulong 8
put buf add sub t 8 j uchar and shr bits mul j 8 255
end
for b ulong div t 64
block mul b 64
end
for k ulong 4
v = get hs k
for j ulong 4
emith uchar and shr v mul uint j 8 255
end
end
emit nl
end
fn main to int
initk
note the empty message, as a slice of length 0
md5 part m0 0 0
md5 m0
md5 m1
md5 m2
md5 m3
ret 0
end
</syntaxhighlight>
